transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm really embarrassed to be here, but I've been struggling with my eating lately. I keep completely losing control and eating massive amounts of food in a very short period, far more than what is normal. It's starting to make me feel really distressed and overwhelmed.
After these episodes of overeating, do you engage in any behaviors to try to prevent weight gain, such as self-induced vomiting, misusing laxatives, or excessive exercising?

Yes, I do, and I feel so ashamed about it. After an episode, I force myself to throw up and often misuse laxatives or diuretics to try and clear my system. I also try to fast for long periods or push myself to exercise way past my physical limits just to burn it all off.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Binge-Eating Disorder, Bulimia Nervosa]. The patient confirmed engaging in compensatory behaviors such as self-induced vomiting, misuse of laxatives and diuretics, and excessive exercise following episodes of binge eating. These compensatory behaviors are the defining clinical distinction of Bulimia Nervosa, ruling out Binge-Eating Disorder.
